doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Dallas memories and the Denver years
title: Denver colleagues and musicians who sat in
summary: Walton says there was little to learn from the Denver players who hired him, such as Shelly Rim and Bob Gray, though visitors like Frank Foster sought him out.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Any other … were there any musicians in, that you were associated with during your time in Denver that influenced you?
Or taught you anything, or that you shedded with with when you … or that you had particular strong relationships with?

Uh…. Not really. Uh, they would hire me … uh, uh, there's one name, Shelly Rim [?]. There's another name, Bob Gray, a guitarist. They would hire me to play with 'em and so uh, but I was pretty much on their level by then, you know. So uh, there wasn't a lot to be learned except the, the time on the bandstand, the time at the piano, and uh, tryin' to, you know, uh represent myself in a good way. I met Frank Foster, he came through. And joined Basie, sought us out and came and sat in. But by this time, I was playin' at another joint, so …. But anyway, you would meet people who would seek you out and if they were interested enough, and uh, play.
